paper_scope: A same-checkpoint study of bit-exact and near-lossless storage formats for trained 3D Gaussian Splatting assets.

contributions.statement: A taxonomy that separates bit-exact, same-checkpoint near-lossless, and retraining-required codecs.
A round-trip protocol combining numerical thresholds, visual audit, provenance, and artifact size.
A five-scene qualification of practical same-checkpoint storage formats.

claims.statement: SPZ 8/8 passed the declared near-lossless gate on all five scenes at 5.572191x to 6.072361x compression and under 0.02 dB absolute PSNR change.
SPZ is universally the best or most lossless 3DGS storage format.
claims.rationale: Lossless and near-lossless formats optimize different objectives; conclusions are restricted to the declared same-checkpoint cohort and gate.

claims.statement: The reported Pareto frontier includes encode time, decode time, peak decode memory, and post-decode rendering cost.
claims.blocking_gate: Measure cold and warm encode/decode latency, peak host/GPU memory, and render-ready upload cost under a frozen storage protocol.

claims.statement: The study covers the strongest retraining-required learned compression methods under official implementations.
claims.blocking_gate: Run official FCGS, HAC/HAC++, GSICO, and other current learned-codec implementations as a separately ranked retraining-required cohort.
